previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and a history of bilateral lower extremity amputations was admitted for shakiness and nausea, symptoms she had previously experienced during urinary tract infections. She had not had her Foley catheter changed in 1.5 weeks, and urinalysis showed bacteria and white blood cells, though she remained afebrile with normal white blood cell count. Symptoms improved rapidly after initial antibiotic administration in the emergency department, suggesting a possible anxiety component or medication effect. Gabapentin, which can accumulate in renal failure and cause tremors, was discontinued during admission and restarted at a lower dose upon discharge. She received scheduled hemodialysis, which improved her renal function and electrolytes. Repeat urine culture showed gram-negative rods and yeast, but due to lack of systemic infection signs, antibiotics were not continued to avoid promoting multidrug-resistant organisms. She was discharged home with services, with follow-up planned for pending culture results and ongoing management of chronic conditions.

Brief Hospital Course:
#Nausea/vomiting: Patient presented with chief complaint of one 
episode of nausea and non-bloody vomiting.  The patient reports 
having taken a cap full of Nyquil to help sleep and then 
vomiting shortly after. Differential initially included 
gastroparesis vs viral gastroenteritis.  The patient had no 
further episodes of vomiting and episode may have been related 
to Nyquil.  Infection seems unlikely as episode was isolated.  
Gastroparesis secondary to diabetes is of concern and may be 
worked up as outpatient if patient is willing to do so.  Utility 
of this study while on chronic narcotic medications may be 
limited.  She was given zofran and ativan as needed for nausea.

#ESRD: ESRD secondary to diabetes on hemodialysis ___. 
Patient lost tunneled HD cathether on day two of admission, it 
fell out while patient was moving.  Peritoneal dialysis was 
attempted for short periods of time, but patient did not 
tolerate the procedure well and had significant abdominal pain.  
There was concern about placing a new dialysis catheter in the 
setting of one bottle of blood cultures growing staph 
epidermidis.  The patient was initially treated with Vancomycin, 
however she lost peripheral IV access and after multiple 
attempts at a peripheral line, she was switched to linezolid.  
The patient remained hemodynamically stable and afebrile.  The 
single positive blood culture was felt to be most likely a skin 
contaminant. A tunneled catheter was placed by ___ after 24 hours 
of negative blood cultures and the patient was restarted on HD 
and vancomycin.

#Bacteremia:  A single blood culture grew staph epidermidis.  
Infectious disease was consulted who recommended Vancomycin and 
workup for endocarditis.  A transthoracic echo was performed 
which did not show evidence of endocarditis, however was a 
limited study.  A transesophageal echo was then performed and 
negative for endocarditis.  Line infection was a concern, but 
the indwelling catheter came out on day two of admission 
eliminating this as a possible source of infection.  The patient 
transitioned to linezolid after losing IV access and then 
switched back to Vancomycin once the HD catheter was replaced.  
She remained hemodynamically stable without fever and was 
discharged with 2 weeks of Vancomycin to be completed at 
hemodialysis.

#UTI: Patient had a dirty urinalysis with leukocytosis and left 
shift concerning for urinary tract infection on admission. Past 
infections have been with either generally sensitive organisms 
or, on ___ cultures, a panresistant k.pneumo sensitive to 
tigecycline and tetracyclines only (resistant to carbapenems, 
colistin, zosyn, etc). The patient did not endorse any symptoms 
of urinary tract infection.  Urine cultures grew E coli; one 
culture with >100K colonies and teh other with ___ colonies. 
 Infectious disease was consulted and felt that this most likely 
represented colonization in a patient with a chronic foley and 
antibiotics were not given.

#Cough: Patient presented with a non-productive cough without 
dyspnea.  A chest x-ray showed no acute cardiopulmonary process. 
 On exam the patient had diffuse wheezing suggestive of 
bronchospasm.  The patient was started on duonebs and albuterol 
with codein and quaifenesin for cough.  Her symptoms resolved at 
the time of discharge.  Etiology felt to be viral upper 
respiratory tract infection with component of reactive airwary 
disease.  

#HTN: Patient had evelated blood pressure on admission.  
Carvedilol was continued and the patient improved with 
hemodialysis.  Elevation likely secondary to some volume 
overload.   

#Type I diabetes:  Patient has Type I diabetes with history of 
poor control.  ___ was consulted for recommendations and her 
sliding scale was adjusted accordingly.  

#Phantom pain: Patient was continued on home dose of oxycodone 
and lidocaine patch.

Transitional Issues:
-Hemodialysis
-2 Weeks of Vancomycin with goal trough of 10 after last 
negative blood culture
-blood cultures pending

radiology_notes.text:
NAME OF THE PROCEDURE:  ___ hemodialysis line.

INDICATION:
___ woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease who just lost
access and needs new hemodialysis line for IV antibiotics and hemodialysis.

CLINICIANS:
Dr. ___, ___ fellow, and Dr. ___, ___ attending and
___ who were present and supervised throughout the whole procedure.

ANESTHESIA:
Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of fentanyl for
a total of 150 mcg and Versed for a total of 3 mg during this intraservice
time of 40 minutes, during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored.  Local anesthesia was provided by 1% lidocaine.

PROCEDURE:
Written informed consent was obtained from the patient after risks, benefits,
alternatives, and indications of the procedure were discussed.  Patient was
transported to the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table. 
The left neck was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A
preprocedure timeout was performed as per ___ protocol.

After anesthetizing the skin and subcutaneous tissues, a micropuncture needle
was inserted into the left external jugular vein under ultrasound guidance. 
Hard copy ultrasound images were saved for reference.  A 0.018 nitinol wire
was advanced into the superior vena cava.  After additional anesthesia, a
small ___ was made in the skin.  The micropuncture needle was exchanged with
micropuncture sheath.  The inner cannula and nitinol wire were removed.  A
0.035 J-wire was advanced into the right atrium.  Appropriate measures were
made for a skin incision four fingerbreadths below the venotomy site.  The
wire was then advanced into the IVC.

Attention was now turned to creation of a subcutaneous tunnel.  After
additional local anesthesia, 1 cm skin incision was made.  A 10 ___
tunneled catheter was placed from the incision to the venotomy site with help
of a metal tunneling device.  The venotomy tract was then dilated with 7 and 9
___ dilators.  The peel-away sheath was passed over the wire.  The wire and
inner cannula were removed, and the catheter was passed through the peel-away
sheath.  The peel-away sheath was subsequently removed while the catheter was
pushed into the right atrium.  This was confirmed with fluoroscopy
demonstrating catheter tip in the right atrium.  Both lumens withdrew blood
and flushed easily.  Catheter was secured with ___ silk sutures.  Venotomy
site was closed with ___ Vicryl.  Dry sterile dressings were applied.  No
immediate post-procedure complications were noted.  Patient tolerated the
procedure well.

IMPRESSION:

Successful placement of a tunneled access catheter through the left external
jugular vein approach.  The tip is located in the right atrium and the
catheter is ready for use.
